title: Linked Lists
instructions: A linked list is a chain of nodes. Each node holds a value AND a pointer to the next node. This is structs and pointers working together — the heart of real C.
struct Node { int value; struct Node *next; };
You reach inside a pointer-to-struct with -> instead of a dot: current->value, current->next.
The last node points to NULL, which marks the end of the chain.
To visit every node, start at the first and keep hopping to current->next until you hit NULL.
This is exactly the pattern used by the List, Queue, and HashTable projects in that GitHub repo.
task: Set the last node's next to NULL to end the list, so it prints 10, 20, 30.
hint:
The last node points to nothing, which is NULL:

    c->next = NULL;
